name: Seyed-Ahmad Ahmadi
headline: Senior Solution Architect - AI in Healthcare | Digital Health, Multimodal AI & Accelerated Infrastructure | NVIDIA
summary:
Senior Solution Architect for AI in Healthcare at NVIDIA.

Trusted advisor to healthcare and life sciences enterprises on AI strategy, digital health platforms, and accelerated compute infrastructure.

I operate at the intersection of research innovation and enterprise-scale deployment, helping organizations:
1. Identify high-impact AI workloads across medical imaging, multimodal clinical data, and generative AI
2. Configure scalable AI factories and AI data platforms, leveraging NVIDIA reference architectures from single-node systems to multi-node and SuperPOD environments. Translate validated workload mappings into optimized, production-ready systems.

Core focus areas:
- Multimodal AI integrating imaging, structured and unstructured clinical data
- LLM-powered digital health workflows (RAG, agentic AI, knowledge-grounded systems)
- AI workload identification, infrastructure sizing, and performance optimization
- Relational and graph-based AI, including geometric deep learning and knowledge graphs
- Translating advanced AI research into scalable clinical decision support

20+ years at the intersection of computer science, neuroscience, and clinical research.
Doctorate in Health Informatics; ~20,000 citations (h-index 31).

Group leader Medical AI (BMBF 01 EO 0901 / YSGII-6)
Topics: Clinical translational of SOTA machine&deep learning models; multimodal data from posture, gait, eye motion, multi-modal imaging and clinical meta-data (demographics, clinical scores); multimodal computer aided diagnosis (CADx); representation learning (sequential/variational/adversarial auto-encoders); geometric deep learning, graph neural networks;

positions.title: Postdoctoral Researcher
positions.description:
Acquisition and coordination of DFG grant “3D freehand ultrasound for Parkinson’s disease diagnosis” (Co-funding by DFG Individual Grant BO 1895/4-1 and Lüneburg association, ~570.000 EUR total funding); Part of "Movement Disorders" research group by Prof. Dr. Kai Bötzel
Topics: Computer-assisted Parkinson's disease diagnosis (CADx), Multi-modal ultrasound+MRI+CT atlasing; post-operative assessment of Deep Brain Stimulation (DBS) neurosurgery; development of deep learning models Hough-CNN and V-Net (>2300 citations) with Dice loss (research and industry standard in medical image segmentation); PhD supervision, teaching at Graduate School of Systemic Neurosciences (GSN) LMU/TUM Munich;

Topics: Medical image analysis, Ultrasound imaging, Magnetic Resonance Imaging, Robot-assisted neurosurgery; Workpackage leader ROBOCAST (EU FP7), Task leader ACTIVE (EU Horizon 2020);
